description: Append-only log of technical decisions made by agents under DA-R10-1. Each entry names the agent session that decided it. Entries already on main may not be edited or removed (the checker compares with the base ref). Not owner approvals; tools/r10/delegated-authority.fsx is a format and scope check, so each new entry also needs review in its PR. DTD-R10-002 was withdrawn before merge (review of PR #136, B1): staging v4.1.5 is the owner's OD-V415-01, not a delegated deferral.

decisions.decision: Workstream ownership: lead session owns integration, Workstreams A (milestones) and C (verification), docs/rehearsal-010-optimization/ and tools/r10/; the contract-first UI session owns Workstream B and proposals/r10-contract-first-ui/; the historical-compatibility session owns Workstream D's minimum v4.1.5 contract and proposals/r10-historical-data-compatibility/.
decisions.rationale: Directive sections 3-7: use existing agents, nonoverlapping ownership, lead owns integration.

decisions.decision: v4.1.5 build: the lead session is accountable for v4.1.5 (the owner named the lead); the historical-compatibility session keeps exclusive hands-on ownership of requirements-compiled/v4.1.5 on PR #135, where its compile is already under way, and the lead independently reviews, verifies and merges it. No second agent edits requirements-compiled/v4.1.5.
decisions.rationale: The owner answered 'You' but asked that it not conflict with other updates. Moving a compile already in progress to another session would put two agents on the same package files; directive section 4/7: exclusive ownership, avoid two agents redesigning the same interface.

decisions.decision: Competition UI roles: keep the v4.1.x role names ui and ui-2 and add ui-3; assign UI-1 (shell), UI-2 (workspace) and UI-3 (hypotheses/evidence) areas by file ownership in project-structure, not by renaming roles to ui-a/ui-b/ui-c. No requirements-compiler change.
decisions.rationale: Renaming roles fails X01 for 65 test files and X18, and changes the AGENT-RULES digest unless the compiler changes (V41Package.fs hard-codes ui; laneOverrides name ui-2). File-level ownership gives the same exclusivity with no compiler change on the critical path.
decisions.evidence: PR #135 (v4.1.5 session report of the X01/X18 failure); PR #134 (COMPETITION-UI-OWNERSHIP)

decisions.decision: v4.1.5 interface design (revision 3): a session writes only under workspaces/demo/causa-app-<run> in the connected repository, a reserved namespace that never names a catalog workspace; WorkspaceAddress.T is private and its role comes only from WorkspaceAddress.catalog and .workingCopy; loads, sessions, timers and machine messages are keyed by InvestigationRef {Address; Id}; a private Writable.T guards write access; the contract change goes to the owner as one coupled request, with staging and the fallback as separate requests.
decisions.rationale: Directive section 6 (smallest contract change) and section 7 (stable shared interfaces). Recorded by the lead on behalf of the deciding session, as that session asked; the deciding session is named below. Revision 3 answers the independent review's finding that the role was asserted by the caller; its re-review is pending and this entry does not claim the guard works. The package contracts themselves are approved by the owner through the v4.1.5 interface request; this entry records only the design choice behind them.

decisions.decision: Folded UI view contract: contract files carry types and signatures only (plus already-reviewed boundary code). Implementation code (validation, navigation, presentation language, identifiers and the like; 153 members in the first fold) moves to its producer's files under the competition UI ownership map, rather than being allowlisted as frozen contract.
decisions.rationale: Contracts freeze what agents share; freezing implementation as contract would make 153 code members owner-approved interface and block ordinary fixes. Signatures-only keeps the contract check meaningful and does not relax it.
decisions.evidence: v4.1.5 session report (19:45 UTC) on the fold; PR #134

decisions.decision: Adopt CTP-001 section 1 (docs/execution/contract-triggered-parallel/ADOPTION-DECISIONS.md) for preparation work and rehearsals on Indy-init: the contract lifecycle with immutable versions and change requests, contract completeness per CONTRACT-SCHEMA.json, single-writer ownership with an independent verifier, event-driven integration with an independent browser test at every integration, real-provider evidence for durable persistence, push once per candidate, and never merging past a red check. tools/execution/ctp-check.fsx is advisory. This does not make CTP-001 the competition execution method, a required gate, or change any frozen package; those remain the owner's decisions listed in section 2 of that file.
decisions.rationale: The owner's directive covers updating preparation scripts, development workflows and non-security governance procedures. CTP-001 was independently reviewed in three rounds (final PASS) and merged as PR #145.
